title: A failed POST destroys the milestone forever — ONCE key is set before the write is confirmed, and flush() never retries
evidence: event(): `if (get(k)) return false; set(k, String(Date.now()));` runs BEFORE `buf.push({...})`. flush(): `var rows = buf.splice(0, MAX_BATCH); post('events', rows, keepalive);` — the return value is discarded and post() ends `.catch(function () { return false; })`. There is no retry queue, no backoff, no 'online' listener. Contrast the game's own ContentLog at chart-quest.html:25874 — 'rows leave the queue ONLY after a confirmed 2xx write (see flush())' — plus chart-quest.html:26056 `window.addEventListener('online', () => { backoff = 0; flush(); })`.
playerImpact: Any tester on mobile who hits a tunnel, a lift, a carrier handover, a 429, or a transient 5xx at the wrong 4-second window permanently loses that funnel stage — the ONCE key is already set, so it can never re-fire, not even on a later session. Estimate 2-5 of 20 testers lose at least one milestone; the ones most likely to lose it are exactly the mobile testers whose data you most need. It fails silently and looks identical to 'that player never got there', which is the one conclusion the Founder Report will draw from it.
fix: In flush(), keep the rows: `var rows = buf.slice(0, MAX_BATCH); post(...).then(function(ok){ if (ok) buf.splice(0, rows.length); else schedule(); })`. And move the ONCE `set(k, ...)` so it is written only after a confirmed 2xx (or, minimally, persist the buffer to localStorage under a `cq_bt_pending` key and drain it on next boot — 15 lines, mirrors ContentLog).
subsystem: Analytics contract & integrity (window.CQTrack + window.CQBeta + beta-ingest + founder_report.py)

title: ?fresh=1 splits one human into two player_ids — the wrapper page has already emitted under the old pid before the game wipes it
evidence: `if (DEV_ALWAYS_FRESH || /[?&]fresh(=|&|$)/.test(location.search)) { ... _rk.forEach(k => { if (/^(cq_|shellTrade)/.test(k)) localStorage.removeItem(k); }); }` at chart-quest.html:1647 — this deletes cq_pid, cq_bt_visits, cq_bt_first_seen and every cq_bt_* ONCE key. It runs at document line 1631, i.e. long before the inlined CQTrack boots at chart-quest.html:27705. But play.html:109 `var CQ_QS = location.search || '';` and play.html:104 load cq-track.js FIRST, so the wrapper has already emitted session_start under the pre-wipe pid. The game then strips ?fresh from its own URL (chart-quest.html:1659) but the parent's location.search is never stripped, so every Restart click wipes again.
playerImpact: Conditional on the invite link. If testers are sent a plain https://playchartquest.com link, zero impact. If any tester receives a ?fresh=1 link — and the project's own standing rule is that every test URL carries ?fresh=1 — that tester registers as two players: one with a lone session_start (dragging the 'Landing page' denominator up) and one with all the milestones, halving every conversion percentage in the funnel table. This is also the most likely explanation for '13 players' against a handful of real humans in the current 113-event dataset.
fix: Either (a) send testers a URL with no ?fresh, or (b) preserve identity across the wipe: in the wipe block, read cq_pid before the loop and write it back after — `const _pid = localStorage.getItem('cq_pid'); ... if (_pid) localStorage.setItem('cq_pid', _pid);`. Option (b) is strictly better because it also keeps ?fresh usable for beginner-mode testing without corrupting the cohort. Note this deliberately keeps the cq_bt_* ONCE keys wiped, which is what you want for a genuine re-run.

title: IDENTITY ASSESSMENT: cq_pid is a random localStorage string with no recovery path
evidence: cq-track.js:66-70 `function pid() { var p = get('cq_pid'); if (!p) { p = 'p-' + Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 12); set('cq_pid', p); } return p; }` — 10 base-36 chars, no server issuance, no cookie, no fingerprint fallback. Milestones are gated on localStorage too: cq-track.js:135-139 `var k = 'cq_bt_' + name; if (get(k)) return false; set(k, String(Date.now()));`. Every get/set is wrapped in safe() (cq-track.js:57-59), so in a storage-denied context localStorage.getItem returns null every time.
playerImpact: Private browsing: get() returns null on every call, so a NEW player_id is minted per event — one tester shatters into dozens of one-event players, and no once-gate ever holds, so every milestone re-fires. Cleared storage or a different browser: a clean new player, silently double-counting one human. iOS Safari evicts script-written storage after ~7 days without interaction — a tester who returns on day 8 of a two-week beta returns as a stranger with all milestone flags reset. Two people on one device: ONE merged record, and the second person's tutorial_started, first trade and boss are never recorded at all because the first person's cq_bt_* flags already exist — their entire playthrough is invisible.
fix: Do not build a fingerprint. For 10-20 named testers the correct fix is a per-tester invite token: send each one https://playchartquest.com/play?t=<slug>, have CQTrack prefer that token over the random pid and persist it, and add `t` to the survey row. That makes identity durable across private mode, cleared storage and a second browser, costs one line in pid(), and lets you say 'Sam never got past the tutorial' by name — which is the whole point of a 20-person closed beta.

title: DELIVERABLE — the master per-player query (verified: executed against production, returns one row per player)
line: 85-106 (the fetch this should replace or supplement)
evidence: Run and confirmed working against ymxppzhczvmiuoncuqqu; returned 14 rows, correctly identifying the mobile tester p-fco306cqen (device=mobile, os=iOS, screen=393x852, first_trade_outcome='win', exit_point='first_trade') and the two ghost ids from finding 2 (exit_point='play_page_only', zero session_end rows). build_version comes back NULL for every row — that column is the proof of finding 4.

Fields it CANNOT fill honestly today: build_version (always NULL — no source exists); session length is emitted as three separate numbers (sum_seconds_all_frames = inflated ~3x, longest_frame_seconds = best available proxy, session_end_rows = how much of it is missing) rather than one trustworthy figure, because one trustworthy figure does not exist until finding 1 is fixed; intro_completed_POSTBOSS is deliberately named to stop anyone reading it as tutorial completion; exit_point is milestone+page granularity only.

with ev as (select * from beta_events),
env as (select player_id, min(ts) first_event_ts, max(ts) last_event_ts, count(distinct session_id) raw_session_ids,
  count(*) filter (where name='session_start' and props->>'page'='index') index_loads,
  count(*) filter (where name='session_start' and props->>'page'='play') play_loads,
  count(*) filter (where name='session_start' and props->>'page' in ('game','chart-quest')) game_loads,
  count(*) filter (where name='session_start' and props->>'page'='survey') survey_loads,
  mode() within group (order by device) device, mode() within group (order by browser) browser,
  mode() within group (order by os) os, mode() within group (order by screen) screen,
  mode() within group (order by viewport) viewport
 from ev group by player_id),
fs as (select player_id, min(props->>'first_seen') first_seen_reported from ev where name='return_visit' group by player_id),
ms as (select player_id,
  min(ts) filter (where name='tutorial_started') tutorial_started_at,
  min(ts) filter (where name='tutorial_completed') intro_completed_at,
  min(ts) filter (where name='first_trade_started') first_trade_at,
  min(ts) filter (where name='first_trade_won') trade_won_at,
  min(ts) filter (where name='first_trade_lost') trade_lost_at,
  min(ts) filter (where name='boss_started') boss_started_at,
  min(ts) filter (where name='boss_defeated') boss_defeated_at,
  min(ts) filter (where name='journal_unlocked') journal_unlocked_at,
  min(ts) filter (where name='journal_discovery_completed') journal_disc_done_at,
  min(ts) filter (where name='beta_completed') beta_completed_at,
  count(*) filter (where name='crash') runtime_errors,
  (array_agg(props->>'message' order by ts) filter (where name='crash'))[1] first_error
 from ev group by player_id),
sl as (select player_id,
  sum(nullif(props->>'seconds','')::int) filter (where name='session_end') sum_seconds_all_frames,
  max(nullif(props->>'seconds','')::int) filter (where name='session_end') longest_frame_seconds,
  count(*) filter (where name='session_end') session_end_rows,
  max(nullif(props->>'completion_seconds','')::int) filter (where name='session_end') completion_seconds
 from ev group by player_id),
sv as (select player_id, min(created_at) survey_at, max(q1_rating) q1_rating, max(q2_hook) q2_hook,
  max(q3_improvement) q3_improvement, max(q4_continue) q4_continue, max(q5_anything) q5_anything,
  max(seconds_taken) survey_seconds from beta_surveys group by player_id)
select e.player_id,
  coalesce(f.first_seen_reported::timestamptz, e.first_event_ts) first_visit_ts,
  e.device, e.browser, e.os, e.screen, e.viewport,
  e.raw_session_ids, e.index_loads, e.play_loads, e.game_loads, e.survey_loads,
  sl.sum_seconds_all_frames, sl.longest_frame_seconds, sl.session_end_rows, sl.completion_seconds,
  (m.tutorial_started_at is not null) tutorial_started,
  (m.intro_completed_at is not null) intro_completed_POSTBOSS,
  case when m.trade_won_at is null and m.trade_lost_at is null then null
       when m.trade_lost_at is null then 'win' when m.trade_won_at is null then 'loss'
       when m.trade_won_at < m.trade_lost_at then 'win' else 'loss' end first_trade_outcome,
  (m.boss_defeated_at is not null) boss_defeated,
  (m.journal_disc_done_at is not null) journal_discovery_completed,
  (m.beta_completed_at is not null) beta_completed,
  (s.survey_at is not null) survey_completed,
  s.q1_rating, s.q2_hook, s.q3_improvement, s.q4_continue, s.q5_anything, s.survey_seconds,
  case when s.survey_at is not null then 'survey_submitted'
       when m.beta_completed_at is not null then 'beta_complete_no_survey'
       when m.journal_disc_done_at is not null then 'journal_discovery'
       when m.boss_defeated_at is not null then 'boss_defeated'
       when m.boss_started_at is not null then 'boss_fight'
       when m.first_trade_at is not null then 'first_trade'
       when m.tutorial_started_at is not null then 'tutorial'
       when e.game_loads > 0 then 'game_loaded_never_started'
       when e.play_loads > 0 then 'play_page_only'
       else 'landing_only' end exit_point,
  m.runtime_errors, m.first_error,
  null::text as build_version   -- MISSING: see finding 4
from env e
left join fs f on f.player_id=e.player_id
left join ms m on m.player_id=e.player_id
left join sl on sl.player_id=e.player_id
left join sv s on s.player_id=e.player_id
order by first_visit_ts;

title: There is no route to the survey except finishing the entire beta — the only testers who can give feedback are the ones who liked it enough to finish
evidence: `grep -rn survey website/*.html website/assets/site.js` matches only play.html (the postMessage handoff), terms.html (prose), and game.html. website/index.html and website/assets/site.js contain zero occurrences of 'survey' or 'feedback'. The only caller is chart-quest.html:27892-27893 `emit('survey_started', {}); openSurvey();` inside the post-Journal-Discovery ceremony.
playerImpact: Of 20 testers, your own prior audit (CHARTQUEST_WEBSITE_BETA_LAUNCH_AUDIT_2026-08-04.md:149 'bounces here never sees Level 1 and never sees the survey') and live data (nobody has reached boss/journal yet) predict maybe 3-6 reach the ceremony. The other 14-17 — the ones whose experience you most need to understand, because they quit — have no way to tell you anything. Every response you receive is from a finisher, so the ratings skew high and 'when did it click?' can never be answered by someone for whom it never clicked. scripts/founder_report.py:325 already anticipates a near-zero survey rate and misattributes it to the handoff.
fix: Add a persistent, low-friction feedback route that does not require completion: a footer 'Tell us what you think' link on index.html and a small link in the play.html top bar. Point it at survey.html with a flag (e.g. survey.html?early=1) that softens the copy ('Didn't finish? Even better — tell us where you stopped') and adds one exit-point question. This is also the storage for the Exit Point / Completion Status fields you already know are missing.

title: A retry after a failed send writes a DUPLICATE survey row — response_id is minted per attempt, so the idempotency the edge function promises does not apply to surveys
playerImpact: The classic mobile case: the row is written server-side but the response is lost (dropped connection, CORS failure, 429 from the shared 120/min rate limit at beta-ingest:40). The tester sees 'That did not send', taps again, and you now hold two beta_surveys rows for one person. With 3-6 responses total, one duplicate is a ~20-30% distortion of your rating mean and your q4_continue counts (founder_report.py:253, 266, 275 all divide by len(surveys)). You will not notice, because both rows look like legitimate distinct responses.
fix: Mint response_id once, at first submit, and persist it in the draft: add `if (!answers.rid) { answers.rid = 'r-' + Date.now().toString(36) + '-' + Math.random().toString(36).slice(2,10); saveDraft(); }` before building `row`, and pass `response_id: answers.rid`. Then every retry — including after a full page reload — collapses onto the same row via the existing ignoreDuplicates upsert.
subsystem: Survey (website/survey.html + CQTrack.survey + beta-ingest survey path + CQBeta handoff)

verified.reason: The core technical claim verifies exactly as quoted. cq-track.js:318-326 mints response_id only when absent, and survey.html:357-364 constructs a brand-new object literal inside the submit handler with no response_id, so every attempt gets a new id. The draft is cleared only on success (survey.html:375), so a post-reload retry re-mints too. beta-ingest/index.ts:158-159 keys survey idempotency solely on response_id, and founder_report.py:253/266/275 (plus :216) aggregate surveys with no dedupe by player_id, and no unique-on-player constraint exists anywhere in the repo. So a duplicate row would double-count. However, the severity and the failure narrative are inflated: two of the three cited trigger paths cannot produce duplicates at all.
verified.correction: Severity should be P2, not P1, and the mechanism is narrower than stated. Corrected statement: "website/survey.html:357 builds a fresh row object on every submit attempt with no response_id, so website/assets/cq-track.js:321 mints a new one each time. The upsert idempotency the edge function promises (supabase/functions/beta-ingest/index.ts:155-159, onConflict 'response_id') therefore does not protect surveys against retries. This only produces a duplicate row in one narrow case: the upsert at index.ts:159 commits but the client never sees the 200 (connection dropped mid-response, tab killed, or the user reloads a seemingly-hung submit and re-sends the localStorage draft, which is cleared only on success at survey.html:375). The finding's other two cited causes are wrong: a forbidden origin returns 403 at index.ts:127 and rate limiting returns 429 at index.ts:144, BOTH before the upsert at :159, so neither writes a row and neither can duplicate. The 120/min limit is also per-IP, unreachable by a single tester. The claim that a duplicate would go unnoticed is also wrong: duplicates share player_id, usually session_id, and carry byte-identical free text, which founder_report.py:279-281 prints verbatim in the report. Real cost: if it fires, founder_report.py has no dedupe (ratings at :253, q4_continue counts at :266-275, and survey-completion pct at :216 all use len(surveys) raw), so one duplicate skews a 3-6 response sample and can push survey completion above 100%. Expected player impact: 0-1 of 20 testers, not a systematic problem. Effort S; the proposed fix (persist the rid in the draft and pass it as response_id) is correct and does not break anything, since shapeSurvey at index.ts:92-93 only requires response_id to be present."

title: No 'already submitted' state: a refresh after success gives a blank resubmittable form, and the second submission writes a row but no survey_submitted event, so the two counts diverge

Worse, the counts silently disagree: beta_surveys grows, survey_submitted does not, and founder_report.py:216 `w(f'| Survey completion | {pct(len(surveys), total)} |')` can report over 100% completion while the funnel table shows fewer submissions than responses.

title: pid() is not memoised, so a private-browsing / storage-blocked tester becomes a new player on every single event
